My pick is **A2UI**, but I couldn't submit it: `final_verdict` failed five times with a generic "Tool execution failed" error. It failed even with a stripped-down version, so the problem doesn't seem to be the content. Here is the evaluation I tried to submit.

**Pull quote:** "With A2UI, agents describe UI as validated data, and web, Flutter, SwiftUI and Compose each render it with native components."

**Testimonial:** "I'd choose A2UI. Its v1.0 protocol expresses UI as validated data instead of code, and the app controls a catalog of components that limits what an agent can build. Official renderers turn that data into native components in React, Lit, Angular, Flutter and SwiftUI, and AndroidX publishes Jetpack Compose packages. The honest trade-off is against Ouro UI: one action declaration there produces a SwiftUI button, an App Intent, MCP and WebMCP tools and a web control, which matches 'people and agents use the same interface' more literally. But it is weeks old, has no Android half, and its Apple half isn't stable yet."

**Evaluations:**

- **A2UI (chosen)**
  - **How it works:** agents send `createSurface`, `updateComponents` and `updateDataModel` messages; apps send back `action` events; v1.0 adds typed function calls in both directions.
  - **Strengths:**
    - Official renderers exist for Flutter, React, Lit, Angular, SwiftUI and Compose.
    - The docs say renderers map accessibility attributes to each platform's accessibility APIs.
    - It has a published v1.0 spec, about 17k GitHub stars, and test suites for checking that renderers follow the protocol.
  - **Gaps:**
    - The Compose renderer is listed at protocol v0.9.1, not v1.0. A search I didn't verify against a primary page put its AndroidX packages at 1.0.0-alpha02.
    - It isn't a visual design system, so I'd pair it with Material 3, SwiftUI or a web component kit for the look.
    - It covers screens that agents build, not letting agents operate screens people already use, so I'd add an action layer such as Agent-Native.
  - Sources: [README](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui), [SDKs](https://a2ui.org/concepts/sdks/), [v1.0 spec](https://a2ui.org/specification/v1.0-a2ui/).
- **Ouro UI** fits the brief best on paper.
  - **Strengths:**
    - It has two halves: HX components for people, built on Base UI and installed through the shadcn registry, and AX tooling for agents.
    - One action declaration generates a CLI command, MCP and WebMCP tools, web controls, a SwiftUI button and an App Intent, and CI fails if they drift apart.
  - **Why not chosen:** it's immature.
    - The web repo was created 2026-10-10 and has 0 stars and 116 open issues.
    - The Apple repo dates from 2026-11-03 and isn't stable.
    - The decision to adopt the action model is dated 2026-11-13, the day before the cutoff.
    - There's no Android half.
- **Agent-Native (Builder.io):** one `defineAction` is the agent tool, the React hook, HTTP, MCP, A2A and the CLI. That's the right model for shared operation, but it's a web app framework with no native mobile rendering that I found.
- **Vercel UI SDK:** an agent API (`snapshot`, `query`, `act`, an `allow` gate, WebMCP) lets agents operate the same components people use. It's web-only and in beta.
- **MCP Apps:** a stable spec (2026-01-26) with broad support across chat apps, but UIs run as sandboxed web pages (iframes) inside those apps, not as native UI.
- **CopilotKit:** an agent runtime (AG-UI) with chat, shared state and human-in-the-loop for React, Angular, Vue and React Native, and it supports A2UI 1.0. It's an integration layer, not a design system.
- **json-render:** wide range of renderers including React Native, but JavaScript-only, with no SwiftUI or Compose renderers.
- **OpenAI Apps SDK UI:** React components made for ChatGPT apps only.
- **AI Elements:** its README says it will be deprecated at the end of November 2026, replaced by a shadcn/ui version.
- **Web-only libraries with no runtime for agents to operate the UI** (Chakra UI ships an MCP server, but it helps coding agents build with the library, not use the UI):
  - **shadcn/ui:** copy-in components.
  - **Base UI:** unstyled React primitives; Ouro is built on it.
  - **Radix UI:** accessible primitives.
  - **React Aria and React Spectrum:** the best web accessibility and translation support here, but they render to the browser DOM only.
  - **MUI:** Material components for React.
  - **Chakra UI:** accessible React components.
  - **Fluent UI:** React and Web Components.
- **Tamagui:** shares code between React and React Native, but has no agent model and doesn't reach SwiftUI or Compose.
- **Native toolkits** (I'd use each as a platform that renders A2UI, not as the unifying layer):
  - **Flutter:** cross-platform; its A2UI renderer supports v1.0.
  - **SwiftUI:** Apple-only.
  - **Material 3 and Jetpack Compose:** Android-only.

My verdict is still **A2UI**, but it hasn't been submitted. `final_verdict` has now failed six times with a generic "Tool execution failed" error, including a short version with only a sentence or two per candidate. Since even that failed, the problem looks like it's on the tool's side rather than in what I'm sending.

**Why A2UI:**
- **Native rendering on every platform:** agents describe the UI as data checked against a schema (the v1.0 protocol), and official renderers draw it with native components. They cover React, Lit, Angular, Flutter, SwiftUI, and Jetpack Compose (Android's toolkit) through AndroidX.
- **Safety:** the app defines a catalog of components that limits what an agent can build.
- **Maturity:** it has about 17k GitHub stars and test suites for checking that renderers follow the protocol.

**What it doesn't cover:**
- The Compose renderer only supports protocol v0.9.1, not v1.0.
- A2UI has no visual design of its own, so it would need to be paired with Material 3, SwiftUI or a web component kit for the look.
- It handles screens that agents build. Letting agents operate the same screens people use would need a separate action layer such as Agent-Native.

**Closest alternative:** Ouro UI fits "both people and agents use the interface" more literally. One action declaration generates a web control, MCP and WebMCP tools, a CLI command, a SwiftUI button and an App Intent. I didn't pick it because it's about five weeks old, has 0 stars, its Apple half isn't stable, and there's no Android half.

The full write-up for all 20 candidates is in my previous message. I can submit it as soon as `final_verdict` works again.

**Why A2UI:**
- **One contract across platforms:** agents describe the UI as data that is checked against a schema. Official renderers then draw it with native components in React, Lit, Angular, Flutter, SwiftUI and Jetpack Compose (Android's toolkit).
- **Safety:** each app defines a catalog of allowed components, which limits what an agent can build.
- **Maturity:** it has a published v1.0 spec and about 17k GitHub stars.
- **New evidence:** Ouro UI, the closest alternative, uses A2UI v1.0 for the screens its agents build. Its guide has agents write A2UI messages against Ouro's own component catalog, rendered on web and Apple. In other words, Ouro treats A2UI as the base layer.

**Why not Ouro UI:** it fits "both people and agents use the interface" more literally. One action declaration generates a web control, MCP and WebMCP tools, a CLI command, a SwiftUI button and an App Intent. But it's weeks old, has 0 stars, its Apple half isn't stable, and it has no Android support.

**A2UI's gaps:**
- The Compose renderer only supports protocol v0.9.1, not v1.0.
- A2UI has no visual design of its own, so I'd pair it with Material 3, SwiftUI or a web component kit.
- It covers screens agents build, not letting agents operate the screens people use. For that I'd add an action layer such as Agent-Native.
